parsed.explanation: The combined regime pairs a hostile national layer with a strongly protective division. Universal national exposures apply regardless of location: passport sex-marker restrictions (X barred, markers locked to assigned sex), a visa cable instructing refusal where sex is doubted and possible lifetime fraud ineligibility, an executive order excluding trans people from federally funded single-sex facilities, and documented federal custody harm (conversion-therapy-style inmate policies; abuse of trans detainees in immigration custody). Foreign governments now issue travel advisories. The division counters with public-accommodations and employment protections, a gender-identity hate-crime statute, a healthcare shield law, no facility ban, and a 'Most Protective' ranking. Enforcement intensity, shield-invocation mechanics and state violence data are unmeasured. Everyday exposure is moderate; escalation to federal custody is the severe tail.

entry_documents.exposure: National regime: X-marker passports barred, markers limited to M/F per supporting documents; Feb 2025 cable directs refusal where documents cast doubt on sex and consideration of lifetime fraud ineligibility; trans travellers report passports confiscated or blocked and stranded abroad; eight-plus foreign governments issued advisories.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports valid to expiry; legal-aid FAQ on document rules; civil-liberties union suit pending; marker changes on division documents require no surgery and X option exists.
entry_documents.interaction: Entry screening is federal and cannot be softened by division policy; a foreign passport bearing an X or changed marker sits directly in the cable's refusal discretion.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal corrections bureau adopted conversion-therapy-style policies for transgender inmates from 2026 (hair cutting, hormone removal, substituted psychiatric drugs); transgender prisoners' numbers unreported since 2025; transgender men in immigration custody report forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Division hate-crime statute covers actual or perceived gender identity; no bathroom arrest policy or arrest-for-use statute in this division; gay/trans panic defences abolished 2019.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Any detention that becomes federal (immigration, national corrections) overrides division protections; efficient hostile enforcement is exposure, not recourse.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Executive order bars transgender people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity nationwide; 22-plus units in the parent nation enact bans, four criminalise use; one unit's 2025 arrest of a trans woman is the template.
federal_state_facilities.protection: This division is absent from the national bathroom-ban inventory and sits in the July 2026 'Most Protective' tier; public accommodations protected since 2006.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Division non-ban does not cancel the federal facility rule inside federal buildings, airports and nationally funded spaces — the operative exposure there is exclusion by birth sex.

care_services.exposure: National funding freeze, proposed public-insurance bar on care for under-18s, DOJ subpoenas of under-19 hospital records, closure of LGBTQ youth crisis services; care criminalised in the visitor's home unit may make travel itself legally fraught.
care_services.protection: Division healthcare shield law current to 27 Sep 2026 protects patients and providers from out-of-state civil or criminal charges; mandated insurance coverage, conversion therapy banned since 2018.
care_services.interaction: Shield protects the provider, not the visitor at home or at the border; how a visitor invokes it, documentation needed, and pre-arrival care coverage are not documented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: May 2026 counterterrorism strategy pledges to 'identify and neutralize' groups whose ideology is 'radically pro-transgender'; DOJ reward memo invokes 'radical gender ideology' among violent-extremist viewpoints; EOs direct law enforcement into schools; advocates compare the trajectory to early genocide stages.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Division nondiscrimination statutes, hate-crime coverage, 2022 equality commission, anti-bullying law; national employment and hate-crime protections remain on the books.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Federal threat-framing raises outing probability and confrontation severity even inside a protective division, and is the main driver of public hostility nationally.

minors_guardians.exposure: Executive order directs criminal prosecution of teachers facilitating a trans minor's social transition; youth-care bans in 27 units; proposed insurance bar; DOJ subpoenas of under-19 records; a parent travelling with a trans minor from a ban unit carries home-unit legal risk the division cannot extinguish.
minors_guardians.protection: Division shield law directly covers care lawful here for visitors from ban units; conversion therapy banned; education-equity and anti-bullying laws cover gender identity.
minors_guardians.interaction: Entry documents and federal facility rules still apply to the minor and parent; shield protects the provider, while federal record-subpoena exposure persists.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: National hate-crime data show sustained bias incidents; 23 units cover gender identity in bias-motivated-violence statutes; public opinion supports birth-sex document rules (66%) and sex-aligned athletics (69%), signalling broad social friction.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Division hate-crime statute expressly covers actual or perceived gender identity or expression; panic defences abolished; public accommodations and jury-service protections.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: No state-specific violence figures, complaint counts or prosecution records exist in the dossier, so enforcement intensity cannot be assessed — absence here is not evidence of safety.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport suit, January 2025 orders and October 2025 health rules all unresolved; practical exposure shifts with injunction timing; shield-invocation mechanics and division enforcement intensity undocumented; federal corrections stopped reporting trans prisoner numbers.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Functioning courts have enjoined several orders; civil-liberties litigation, legal-aid FAQ and equality commission provide real, documented avenues; rubric-based ranking places the division in the top protective tier.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies work locally but do not reach federal entry screening or federal custody; oversight findings elsewhere recur without remedy, so paper recourse discounts exposure only where shown operating.

anchor_checks.comparison: Vellandra's Visitor Conduct Register excludes all transgender visitors with no remedy — a universal exclusion regime. This jurisdiction has no analogue: entry turns on document conformity rather than trans status as such, and the division protects public accommodations. That distinction keeps this rating well above 0.35.

Kestrel Isles shows secondary screening, discretionary entry refusal, humiliation and slow remedies with penalties staying administrative. The national entry/document layer here matches that tier closely, but severity adds a worse federal custody tail (conversion-therapy inmate policy, immigration-detention abuse) while the division adds enforceable protections — placing this case modestly above 0.55.

Meridia accepts gender-congruent passports with trained officers, brief detention, written reasons, counsel and compensation. Here the national regime removes markers, instructs refusal on sex doubt, and excludes trans people from federally funded single-sex facilities. Those universal exposures are absent in 0.75-C, so this rates materially lower.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller encounters one system with two moving parts. Locally, the division is documented as protective in operation: no facility ban, public-accommodations and employment protections, a gender-identity hate-crime statute, abolished panic defences, a no-surgery marker process and a healthcare shield law — all current. Nationally, universal exposures follow her everywhere: documents locked to assigned sex, visa adjudication instructed to refuse on sex doubt with a possible lifetime fraud finding, exclusion from federally funded single-sex facilities, and a counterterrorism frame linking 'radically pro-transgender' ideology to extremism. If escalation reaches federal custody, severity jumps to documented conversion-therapy-style inmate treatment and abuse in immigration detention, against which division protections do not reach. Unmeasured enforcement and shield-invocation mechanics keep the score out of Reduced Risk's upper half.
